name: deckard-notes
description: Your notes, tasks, and people, connected and kept local. Find what you wrote, chase down loose ends, and retire what's done.

colors.description: Background behind the tagged section or task the cursor is in, in Markdown notes.
Left edge of the tagged section or task the cursor is in, in Markdown notes.
Color of an in-progress task's box in the editor, such as [/].
Color of an overdue task's due date in the editor, and of the "overdue 5 days" hint after its line.
Color of the hints after a task's line in the editor, such as "due today" and "needs a new date".

walkthroughs.title: Get started with Deckard
walkthroughs.description: Index the Markdown notes you already write, then follow the people, projects, and tasks in them.

steps.title: Write a note
steps.description:
Deckard reads every saved Markdown file in the workspace. Start today's note and write a line or two: a / at the start of a line offers a task, a heading, a link, a table of tasks, or one of your templates. Or make a work sample: a week of a team lead's notes, to try everything on.
[Create today's note](command:deckard.createDailyNote)
[Create a work sample](command:deckard.createWorkSample)

steps.title: Tag it, and mention a person
steps.description:
Write a tag such as #project/atlas on a heading or a task to say what it is about, and @dana to say who. Cmd-click (Ctrl-click on Windows and Linux) a tag or a person to see every note and task that carries it.
[Open Help](command:deckard.showHelp)

steps.title: Link two notes
steps.description:
Write [[ and the start of another note's name to link it. That note then lists this one under Linked from, in the Context view and on its page, so a decision finds its meeting and a person finds every 1:1.
[Open the Context view](command:deckard.relatedNotes.focus)

steps.title: Find anything
steps.description:
Find (Ctrl+Shift+Alt+F; Cmd+Shift+Alt+F on macOS) searches as you type. A search page holds the whole result, and Refine narrows it. Write words, #tags, is:open, or updated >= 7d, joined with AND, OR, and NOT.
[Find a note](command:deckard.searchWorkspace)

media.altText: A search page with its results and Refine beside them.

steps.title: Add a task
steps.description:
Write a task from anywhere: Add Task (Ctrl+Shift+Alt+N; Cmd+Shift+Alt+N on macOS) adds it to the note you are in, or to today's note when none is open, and reads a date or a priority from its last words, such as "call Rhea friday".
[Add a task](command:deckard.addTask)
[Open the Tasks view](command:deckard.agenda.focus)

media.altText: The Tasks view listing overdue, today's, and upcoming tasks beside a daily note.

steps.title: See the workspace
steps.description:
Home collects what is due today, what slipped, your tasks, and the notes you opened lately. Customize Home, beside its tabs, adds, resizes, and reorders the widgets.
[Open the Dashboard](command:deckard.showDashboard)

media.altText: Home, with today's note, the Tasks view's list, and favorite tags as widgets.

viewsWelcome.contents:
Hub notes and the notes about their tags appear here, as pages under the pages they belong to.

A hub note describes a tag with describes: in its front matter, such as describes: project/atlas. A note is filed under it when its front matter or first heading carries the tag, or when it says up: "[[Atlas]]".
[Read about hub notes](https://deckard.esperinnovations.com/search-pages.html#hub-notes)

Open a Markdown note to see its headings here.
[Create today's note](command:deckard.createDailyNote)
[Open Help](command:deckard.showHelp)

Your open tasks appear here, grouped by when they are wanted.

Write one in a note as a checklist item, or add one from anywhere.
[Add a task](command:deckard.addTask)
[Open the Task Board](command:deckard.showTaskBoard)

The Tasks view lists only the tasks its search finds, and none match now.
[Show every open task](command:deckard.clearAgendaQuery)
[Edit the search](command:deckard.agenda.editQuery)

commands.title: Open Notes Graph Around This Note
Move Inline Tags to Front Matter
Edit What the Tasks View Lists…
Tidy Favorites, Pins, and Saved Searches
Restore Favorites, Pins, and Searches from a Copy

view/item/context.when: view == deckard.hubs && (viewItem == hubNote || viewItem == hubChild) && config.deckard.openNotesIn == page
view == deckard.hubs && (viewItem == hubNote || viewItem == hubChild) && config.deckard.openNotesIn != page

languageModelTools.name: deckard_query
languageModelTools.userDescription: Search the workspace's Markdown notes and tasks with a Deckard query.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Searches the user's local Markdown notes and checklist tasks, as indexed by the Deckard extension, with a Deckard query, and returns the matching note sections and tasks with their workspace-relative paths, one-based lines, and headings; tasks include their state, due date, and priority. Use it to answer questions about the user's notes, projects, people, and to-dos. For example, 'open tasks for Atlas' is tag = #project/atlas AND task = open, and 'what is overdue' is task = open AND due < today. Conditions combine with AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses. Fields: tag (tag = #project/atlas; tag = #risk/* matches a namespace; a bare #tag or @person also works), text (text ~ "vendor" matches words in note and task text), link (link = [[Note]] or a bare [[Note]] finds entries that link to a note; [[Note#Heading]] one heading), task (open, done, or any; only tasks match), due, scheduled, and start (a date such as 2026-09-20, today, tomorrow, a weekday such as friday, a phrase such as "oct 3" or end-of-month, this-week, next-month, a window such as 7d counted forward, or none), done (done = 7d means completed in the last seven days), priority (highest, high, medium, none, low, lowest; priority >= high), kind (an entity namespace such as project or person), file and path (with * and ? wildcards), created and updated (dates, a weekday such as friday meaning the last one, this-week, last-month, a month such as 2026-08, or windows such as 30d). Shorthands: is:open, is:done, is:overdue, is:due (open and due within seven days), is:today (what the Tasks view lists under Today), is:needs-date (open and more than 30 days past due), is:task, is:note, is:waiting (on hold, as [w] Waiting, [s] Someday, or [=] Blocked, or assigned to someone else), is:available (open, not blocked, started, not on hold), is:daily and is:periodic (written in a daily note, or a daily, weekly, or monthly note), has:due and no:due (also scheduled, start, done, priority), and in:folder for a folder and everything in it. Operators are = != ~ !~ > >= < <=. If you do not know a tag's exact name, call deckard_list_tags first.

query.description: A Deckard query, such as tag = #project/atlas AND task = open.

limit.description: The most notes, and the most tasks, to return. Defaults to 25; totals always count every match.

sort.description: Order by title, or newest created or updated first. Otherwise tasks are listed open first and soonest due first.

languageModelTools.name: deckard_list_tags
languageModelTools.userDescription: List the tags used in the workspace's Markdown notes, most used first.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists the tags in the user's local Markdown notes, as indexed by the Deckard extension, most used first, with how many entries use each. Tags look like #project/atlas, #topic/leadership, or @person-name. Use it to find the exact tag to pass to deckard_query, optionally narrowed by a search such as 'atlas' or 'project/'.

search.description: Only tags whose name contains this text, such as atlas or project/.

limit.description: The most tags to return. Defaults to 50.

languageModelTools.name: deckard_add_task
languageModelTools.displayName: Add a task to a Deckard note
languageModelTools.userDescription: Adds a task to today's note, or to a note you name, after showing you the line.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Adds a checklist task to one of the user's Markdown notes: to today's daily note, or to the note named by a workspace-relative path as deckard_query reports paths. Write the task's words as text; metadata may be written in them the way the user writes tasks, such as a due date 📅 2026-09-30, a priority ⏫, or a person 👤 @dana. Nothing is written until the user approves the exact line in a preview; the answer says whether it was written, and where. Use deckard_change_task to change a task that already exists.

text.description: The task's words, such as "Call Ren about the budget 📅 2026-09-30".

note.description: A workspace-relative note to add it to, such as notes/atlas.md. Today's daily note when absent.

languageModelTools.name: deckard_change_task
languageModelTools.displayName: Change a task in a Deckard note
languageModelTools.userDescription: Completes, reopens, retitles, dates, prioritizes, or hands over a task, after showing you the line.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Changes one existing checklist task, named by its note and one-based line as deckard_query reports them. Any of: title (new words), complete (true or false), due (YYYY-MM-DD, or null to clear), priority (highest, high, medium, low, lowest, or null to clear), assignee (a person tag such as @dana, or null to clear). Only the fields given change; the rest of the line is kept as written. The change is refused if the line is no longer the task the index knows, so ask deckard_query first. Nothing is written until the user approves the exact line in a preview; the answer says whether it was written.

note.description: The task's note, workspace-relative, as deckard_query reports it.

line.description: The task's one-based line, as deckard_query reports it.

complete.description: true completes it, writing the done date; false reopens it.

status.description: A status to set, by its name, as "In progress", "Waiting", or "Cancelled", or by its character in brackets, as "[/]". Done completes it, as complete does.

due.description: A day as YYYY-MM-DD, or null to clear the due date.

priority.description: The priority, or null to clear it.

assignee.description: Who the task is for, as their tag, or null to clear it.

deckard.notesFolder.description: Optional workspace-relative folder containing Markdown notes. Leave empty to index all Markdown files in the workspace.

enumDescriptions: A note or task opens in the editor, at its line.
A note or task opens on the note page, a Deckard page that draws the note with its links, tags, tasks, and query blocks working, scrolled to its line.
deckard.openNotesIn.markdownDescription: Where a note or task opens from Deckard's pages, the Hubs view, Find, and the breadcrumb lens. **Shift**-click, or Shift+Enter, opens it the other way. A link followed in the editor, the Tasks view, and the Outline stay in the editor.

enumDescriptions: A plain interface that takes its colors and fonts from your VS Code theme, light or dark.
Deckard's original replicant terminal interface.
A dark technical operations interface inspired by the Oblivion reference screens.
A warm, high-contrast interface inspired by LCARS from Star Trek: The Next Generation.
A neon grid interface inspired by 1980s synthwave and outrun aesthetics.
A flight-display interface inspired by F-14 Tomcat HUD instrumentation.
A woodland travel-journal interface inspired by The Lord of the Rings.
A spare mission-control interface inspired by the Endurance and TARS in Interstellar.
deckard.theme.description: Visual theme used by Deckard webviews.

enumDescriptions: Deckard as it ships: each theme's decoration, display headings, every helper line, raised cards, tag chips, counts, and dates written both ways.
Each theme's decoration and the lines that teach turned off, and tags drawn as text, at the usual spacing.
Also compact spacing, flat cards, no counts beside names, and dates as how far off.
deckard.display.level.description: How much every Deckard page draws: Full, Quiet, or Zen. Every Display setting follows it while it is Auto. Your own choice, the same in every workspace.

enumDescriptions: Follows Display: styled at Full, plain at Quiet and Zen.
Each theme's decoration and display type: backdrops, glows, cut corners, shadows, metric codes, and headings in capitals.
The same colors and fonts, without decoration, headings in sentence case, and thinner edges. Corpo is already plain.
deckard.display.themeStyling.description: Each theme's decoration and display type, or the theme drawn plain.

enumDescriptions: Follows Display: shown at Full, hidden at Quiet and Zen.
Lines that teach: the search box's syntax line, Refine's hint, and Home's hint bar.
Those lines hidden. A search's error message always shows.
deckard.display.helpText.description: Lines that teach rather than show: the search box's syntax line, Refine's hint, and Home's hint bar.

enumDescriptions: Follows Display: comfortable at Full and Quiet, compact at Zen.
The usual spacing, and 30px controls.
Tighter spacing, and 26px controls; never under 24px targets.
deckard.display.density.description: How much room pages leave between things.

enumDescriptions: Follows Display: raised at Full and Quiet, flat at Zen.
Each card is a raised panel inside its border.
Rows parted by a divider, lifting onto the card surface under the pointer and keyboard focus.
deckard.display.cardFrames.description: How cards and rows are drawn on every Deckard page. Your own choice, the same in every workspace.

enumDescriptions: Follows Display: chips at Full, text at Quiet and Zen.
Each tag in a tag list is a small framed button.
Each tag is plain text in the theme's tag color, its # or @ kept, underlined under the pointer, with a focus ring from the keyboard.
deckard.display.tags.description: How tags are drawn where they are listed on their own, such as a note card's tags and Refine; a tag inside a title is always text. Either way a tag opens its page. Your own choice, the same in every workspace.

enumDescriptions: Follows Display: shown at Full and Quiet, hidden at Zen.
The number beside each name: a widget's total, a group's count, a column's tasks, a tab's results.
Those numbers left out of sight. A screen reader still reads each one, and figures that are the point, such as Home's Due today, always show.
deckard.display.counts.description: Whether pages draw the counts beside names. Your own choice, the same in every workspace.

fileAndLine.description: The file and line an entry is written in, and the headings above it.

created.description: When a note or task was created: a task's ➕ date, or its note's.

updated.description: When a note, or a task's note, was last changed.

deckard.display.cardDetails.description: Which details pages draw under an entry while the pointer is on it or it has focus: its file and line, and its created and updated dates. Untick all three to draw none; a screen reader still reads the file and line. A task's created date is its own ➕ date when it has one, else its note's; its updated date is its note's. Your own choice, the same in every workspace.

enumDescriptions: Follows Display: both at Full and Quiet, how far off at Zen.
How far off and the date: "Overdue 2 days · 2026-10-02".
Only how far off: "Overdue 2 days". A date over a month away still shows.
The date with its state: "Overdue · 2026-10-02".
deckard.display.dates.description: How pages write a task's due date. An overdue date always says Overdue, and a screen reader hears the whole date either way. Your own choice, the same in every workspace.

deckard.display.dateFormat.markdownDescription: How Deckard writes a date for you to read: on pages, in views, in messages, and in the task editor. Written with the tokens Obsidian's daily notes use, such as `YYYY-MM-DD`, `DD/MM/YYYY`, `D MMM YYYY`, or `ddd, MMM D, YYYY`; `L` and `LL` are your display language's own forms, and text in `[brackets]` is written as it is. Dates written into notes, file names, and searches stay `YYYY-MM-DD`. Empty, or a format with no date in it, reads as `YYYY-MM-DD`. [Choose Date Format…](command:deckard.chooseDateFormat) shows each with today's date. Your own choice, the same in every workspace.

deckard.display.shortDateFormat.markdownDescription: How Deckard writes a day of this year where there is little room: the Tasks view's day headings, the Pages view, the calendar's day title, search completions, and Linked from. A day in another year is written in `#deckard.display.dateFormat#`. The same tokens, such as `ddd, D MMM` or `D/M`. Empty, or a format with no date in it, reads as `ddd, MMM D`. Your own choice, the same in every workspace.

deckard.dashboard.openOnStartup.description: Open the Deckard Dashboard when VS Code starts in a workspace with indexed notes.

enumDescriptions: Weeks run Sunday to Saturday.
Weeks run Monday to Sunday.
Weeks start on the day VS Code's display language starts them.
deckard.calendar.weekStart.markdownDescription: The day a week starts on: in the Calendar, in weekly notes and their reviews, in a search's `this-week`, `last-week`, and `next-week`, and in *next week* and *end of week* typed as a date. A weekly note written before a change still opens for the week it mostly covers.

deckard.calendar.exportFile.markdownDescription: A calendar file (`.ics`) Deckard keeps up to date with your dated tasks, for a calendar app to subscribe to: each task an all-day event on its due date, or its scheduled date when it has no due date. A relative path is in the first workspace folder, such as `.deckard/tasks.ics`, and may not climb out of it; `~` is your home folder. It must end in `.ics`, and Deckard never writes over a file that is not a calendar. Empty writes no file; `Deckard: Export Tasks as Calendar…` writes one once.

deckard.calendar.exportQuery.markdownDescription: The search whose dated tasks the calendar file holds, such as `is:open is:mine` or `#project/atlas is:open`. Empty is every open task.

deckard.periodicNotes.folder.description: The folder, inside the notes folder, that new daily, weekly, and monthly notes are written to, such as journal/{yyyy} for one folder a year ({mm} is the month). Empty writes them at the top of the notes folder. Notes already written elsewhere are still found and read.

deckard.periodicNote.review.markdownDescription: Write a review into a newly created weekly or monthly note: what was completed, what is still open, what is coming up next, the notes written and changed, and the tags first seen in that period. [Write a Review](command:deckard.writeReview) writes or updates one whenever you ask.

deckard.periodicNote.reviewSections.markdownDescription: Sections of your own at the end of a review, each a title and a Deckard search, such as `{ "title": "Waiting on others", "query": "is:waiting" }`. Written as a plain list when the review is written, so it says what was true then.

enumDescriptions: Create today's note from the template alone.
Move the unfinished tasks into today's note, under Carried over.
Copy them into today's note and mark each one left behind [>] with a link to today, as a bullet journal does.
Older name for migrate.
deckard.dailyNote.rollover.markdownDescription: What a newly created daily note does with the unfinished tasks of the last one. [Roll Unfinished Tasks Forward](command:deckard.rollTasksForward) does the same thing whenever you ask for it.

deckard.templatesFolder.markdownDescription: Folder of note templates, relative to the workspace folder. [New Note from Template](command:deckard.newNoteFromTemplate) lists its Markdown files, and Deckard does not index them. `Daily.md`, `Weekly.md`, and `Monthly.md` here, when you add them, are what a new daily, weekly, or monthly note starts from. Leave it empty to turn templates off.

deckard.exclude.markdownDescription: Glob patterns of files and folders Deckard leaves out of its index, written like `#files.exclude#`. Each pattern is relative to the workspace folder and applies when set to `true`, and a pattern that matches a folder leaves out everything in it. Deckard also leaves out what `#files.exclude#` and `#search.exclude#` hide, such as `node_modules`; set one of those patterns to `false` here to index it anyway.

deckard.parked.folders.markdownDescription: Glob patterns of folders and notes Deckard parks, written like `#deckard.exclude#`. A parked note stays indexed and searchable — `is:parked` finds it, and Find and search pages list it last — but is left out of the Tasks view, the status bar, the Task board, rollover, the calendar, Related Notes, the Notes Graph, and tag completion. Each pattern is relative to the workspace folder and applies when set to `true`; a pattern that matches a folder parks everything in it. `#deckard.exclude#` wins: an excluded note is not indexed at all.

deckard.parked.tags.markdownDescription: Tags that park whatever carries them: a note whose front matter has one, a heading and everything under it, or a task. A tag parks its sub-tags too, so `project/old` parks `#project/old/phase-1`. **Park Note** writes the first of these into the note's front matter. Parked items stay searchable with `is:parked`.

enumDescriptions: A tagged line is a note of its own.
Only headings are notes. A tagged line keeps its tags and its place, and the heading holding it is what a search returns.
As Heading, except a line marked with a ^block-id, which stays a note of its own.
deckard.noteBoundaries.description: Where one note ends and the next begins inside a Markdown file. Tasks are always their own entry, wherever they are written.

deckard.entityNamespaceAliases.description: Maps one #namespace to another. Targets can be built-in or custom; for example, { "proj": "project", "leadership": "management" } treats #proj/atlas as a project and collapses #leadership/performance into #management/performance.

deckard.highlightNoteSections.markdownDescription: Highlight the tagged section or task the cursor is in, in Markdown notes. Its colors are `deckard.sectionHighlightBackground` and `deckard.sectionHighlightBorder`.

enumDescriptions: Everything Deckard draws in the editor: counts, hints, previews, and lenses.
What helps with tasks, and what reports a problem; no link counts, mention lenses, or breadcrumbs.
A quiet page for writing: the / menu, hover previews, and problem reports only.
deckard.editor.preset.description: What Deckard draws in the editor, as one choice. A deckard.editor.* setting you change yourself wins over it.

deckard.editor.referenceCounts.description: Show, above the lines of a Markdown note, how many notes link to it, how many links name each heading, how many open tasks sit under each heading, and how many related entries Related Notes finds for each tagged heading.

deckard.editor.hoverPreviews.description: Preview the note or section a [[Wiki link]] points at when hovering it, and summarize a tag's entries when hovering the tag.

deckard.editor.linkDiagnostics.description: Mark a [[Wiki link]] that opens no note, because no note has its name or several do, and offer to create a missing note.

deckard.editor.taskDependencies.description: Show, above a task with ⛔ or 🆔, how many open tasks it waits on and how many it holds up, and name a ⛔ id no task carries. A task with nothing open on either side shows nothing.

deckard.editor.dailyNoteActions.description: Show, above a daily note, links to the daily notes before and after it, and on today's note an action that carries in the unfinished tasks earlier daily notes still hold.

deckard.editor.linkProblems.description: Show, on a note's first line, how many of its [[Wiki links]] open no note, and an action that creates the notes the missing ones name. A note whose links all open a note shows nothing.

deckard.editor.embedProblems.description: Show, above an ![[embed]] the Markdown preview cannot draw, which heading or ^marker went missing, and open the note it names. An embed that draws shows nothing.

deckard.editor.unlinkedMentions.description: Show, on a note's first line, how many other notes write its title or an alias as plain text without linking to it, and an action that links them. A note no other note names shows nothing.

enumDescriptions: [[Atlas]], as Obsidian writes them.
[Atlas](projects/Atlas.md), which GitHub, MkDocs, and other Markdown renderers show as links.
deckard.links.style.description: How a link Deckard makes from a mention is written. Deckard reads both kinds either way.

deckard.editor.slashMenu.description: Offer, after a / typed alone at the start of a line in a note, what to write there: a task, a heading, a link or an embed, today's note, a query block, a table of notes or tasks, or one of your templates.

deckard.editor.stepProgress.description: Show, above a task with steps, a bar of how many of its steps are done and which is next; selecting it goes to the next open step.

deckard.editor.breadcrumbs.description: Show, on a note's first line, where it sits under its hub notes, such as Projects › Atlas › Vendor review, as the Hubs view files it; selecting it opens the note above. A note no hub holds shows nothing.

deckard.editor.hubProgress.description: Show, on a hub note's first line, how far along the tasks of the tag it describes are: how many are done, how many are overdue, and when the next is due. A tag with no task shows nothing.

deckard.editor.dimTaskMetadata.description: Draw a task's dates, priority, repeat rule, ids, and person, and a line's ^block id, fainter than its words, so the sentence reads first. An overdue date is never dimmed.

deckard.editor.taskDueHints.description: Say after an open task's line when it is overdue, due today, or needs a new date, such as "overdue 5 days".

deckard.editor.repeatDiagnostics.description: Mark a 🔁 repeat rule Deckard cannot read, since completing that task would not start the next one, and offer the nearest rule it can read.

enumDescriptions: Obsidian Tasks emoji format, such as 📅 2026-09-20 ⏫ 🔁 every week.
Obsidian Tasks Dataview format, such as [due:: 2026-09-20] [priority:: high] [repeat:: every week].
deckard.tasks.metadataFormat.description: Format Deckard writes for a task that has no metadata yet, in / suggestions and completion dates. A task that already uses one format keeps it, and Deckard reads both.

deckard.me.description: Who you are in your notes, such as @ren-kade, so is:mine finds the tasks that name you as well as the ones for nobody in particular. Empty means is:mine finds only the latter.

deckard.tasks.needsNewDateAfterDays.description: How many days past its due date an open task stays in Overdue. After that it moves to the Tasks view's folded Needs a new date group, and leaves the status bar's count and its warning color. 0 keeps every overdue task in Overdue.

deckard.taskReminderTime.patternErrorMessage: Write a time of day as HH:MM, or leave it empty for no reminder.
deckard.taskReminderTime.description: A time of day, such as 09:00, at which Deckard says how many tasks are due. Empty means no reminder.

deckard.agenda.query.description: A Deckard search that says which open tasks the Tasks view, Home's agenda, and the status bar's count are of, such as is:mine, is:available for what can be started now, or has:due OR has:scheduled OR has:start to leave out undated tasks. Empty means every open task.

deckard.board.limits.description: Work-in-progress limits for board columns, by status, its name with a hyphen for a space, such as { "in-progress": 3 }, or by column, such as { "priority:high": 5 }. A column over its limit shows its count against it, 5 / 3, with a neutral outline. A drop is never refused.

symbol.description: The character between the brackets, as [/].

name.description: What the status is called, in search (status:in-progress), on the board, and to a screen reader.

enumDescriptions: Open, to do.
Open, being worked on.
Open, waiting: left out of is:available.
Done: counts as done everywhere.
Closed, but not done: left out of progress and of what is open.
Not a task: the line stays text, as a pro and con list's.

next.description: The character a click moves it to, when deckard.tasks.checkboxClick is workflow.

icon.description: An icon an open status adds to its box.

deckard.tasks.statuses.markdownDescription: What each checkbox character means, as Obsidian Tasks' statuses do: `- [/]` in progress, `- [w]` waiting, `- [s]` someday, `- [=]` blocked, `- [-]` cancelled. Each has its `symbol`, a `name`, and a `type` (`todo`, `inProgress`, `onHold`, `done`, `cancelled`, or `nonTask`). A task's status is its box's character alone: a `#status/…` tag is a tag like any other. A character no status names is a task to do, called Unknown. `[ ]` and `[x]` are always Todo and Done.

enumDescriptions: Checking a box marks the task done, whatever its status; unchecking a done or cancelled task reopens it as [ ].
A click moves a task to its status's next status, as Obsidian Tasks does, so a task can step from to do to in progress to done.
deckard.tasks.checkboxClick.markdownDescription: What a click on a task's box does, in a page, the Markdown preview, and the Tasks view. **Deckard: Toggle Task Done** always goes to done and back. Set other statuses with **Deckard: Set Task Status…** or the Task board.

deckard.tasks.suggestSteps.markdownDescription: Offers **Suggest steps** in Break into Steps… when a VS Code language model, such as GitHub Copilot, is installed. Only the task's words are sent, to that model, and only when you choose it. Turn off to never offer it.

deckard.assistantTools.description: Let AI assistants in VS Code, such as GitHub Copilot in agent mode, use Deckard's tools: search your notes and tasks with Deckard queries, list your tags, add a task to a note, and change an existing task. VS Code asks before the first call in each session and before each write, and nothing is written until you approve the line in the refactor preview. Deckard sends nothing itself; what a tool returns goes to the assistant that asked.

deckard.mcpServer.enabled.markdownDescription: Run a Model Context Protocol server on 127.0.0.1 so Claude Code and other MCP clients can use Deckard's tools: search your notes and tasks, list your tags, add a task to a note, and change an existing task. A client's write has no dialog of its own, but nothing is written until you approve the line in the refactor preview. It answers only requests that carry its token. [Copy MCP Server Setup](command:deckard.copyMcpSetup) copies the command that adds it; the port is `#deckard.mcpServer.port#`.

deckard.mcpServer.port.description: The port Deckard's MCP server listens on, on 127.0.0.1.
